chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'An-Nahr' (sacrificing by cutting the throat from the front) is in the 'Labbah' (upper chest), and 'Adh-Dhabh' (slaughtering by cutting the windpipe and veins) is in the 'Halq' (throat).

key_terms.الذَّبْحُ: Slaughtering by cutting the windpipe and veins, specifically in the throat.
key_terms.اللَّبَّةِ: The upper part of the chest, the site for Nahr.
key_terms.النَّحْرُ: Sacrificing by cutting the throat from the front, specifically in the upper chest.
key_terms.الْحَلْقِ: The throat, the site for Dhabh.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Nahr and Dhabh in Islamic animal slaughter?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the precise anatomical distinctions between 'Nahr' (cutting the upper throat/labyrinth) and 'Dhabh' (cutting the throat), which is crucial for validating the ritual slaughter of animals according to Shia fiqh. This distinction ensures that the major vessels in the neck are severed correctly, reflecting the Prophet's tradition and the Imams' detailed guidance on ritual purity and law.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘النَّحْرُ’ the sacrificing is in the upper chest, and ‘الذَّبْحُ’ the slaughtering is in the throat’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Al-Nahr is slaughtering from the upper part of the chest (applicable to camels only) and al-Dhabh is slaughtering from the throat.’”
